Romance.focus: Romantic chemistry drives everything. Readers want emotional highs—the butterflies, the jealousy, the 'finally!' moments. Build sexual/romantic tension early and sustain it. Include intimate moments (physical touch escalates naturally: hand-holding → hugging → kissing). Emotional beats matter: misunderstandings create conflict, grand gestures resolve them. Every few chapters, give readers a sweet or steamy payoff. Think: protective moments, jealous scenes, forced proximity, emotional vulnerability.

Urban.focus: Modern city life with high stakes. Focus on career ambition, social climbing, and money/power dynamics. Include specific details: luxury brands, expensive restaurants, penthouse apartments, corporate boardrooms. Conflicts often involve workplace rivalry, class differences, or reputation. Payoffs include: career victories, public face-slapping of competitors, going from broke to wealthy, proving doubters wrong. Ground everything in contemporary reality—no magic, just hustle and strategy.

Fantasy.focus: Magic or supernatural elements shape the world. Establish clear rules: how magic works, what costs it has, who can use it. Power progression is key—protagonist grows stronger through training, discovering abilities, or gaining artifacts. Include epic battles, magical academies, mythical creatures, prophecies. Readers want: underestimated hero proving their worth, mastering forbidden magic, defeating powerful enemies, discovering hidden heritage. Balance world-building with action—don't info-dump, reveal through conflict.

Sci-Fi.focus: Technology and science drive the plot. Whether it's space exploration, AI, cyberpunk cities, or time travel, make the tech feel real and consequential. Include: futuristic gadgets, space battles, hacking, genetic engineering, alien encounters. Conflicts arise from tech gone wrong, corporate control, or survival in harsh environments. Readers want: clever use of technology to solve problems, humanity vs machines, discovering alien secrets, surviving dystopia. Keep scientific logic consistent.

Mystery.focus: Puzzle-solving and clue-gathering drive reader engagement. Plant red herrings early, reveal clues gradually. Every chapter should answer one question while raising two more. Include: crime scenes, interrogations, hidden evidence, suspects with secrets. Structure around reveals: small discoveries build to shocking truths. Protagonist should be observant and clever. Readers want: 'aha!' moments, twist endings, satisfying justice when the mystery unravels. Maintain tension—no one is safe.

Horror.focus: Atmosphere and dread build slowly, punctuated by shock moments. Use isolation, darkness, and the unknown. Include: creepy settings (abandoned houses, dark forests), supernatural threats, psychological terror, body horror hints (not graphic). Balance quiet dread with jump scares. Readers want: spine-tingling suspense, characters making smart choices (not dumb horror tropes), creative scares, survival against impossible odds. Hint at gore rather than describing it explicitly. Make readers afraid to turn the page but unable to stop.

Crime.focus: Law enforcement or criminal activity drives the plot. Include: police procedures, heists, investigations, undercover work, courtroom drama. Realism matters—how cops actually work, legal processes, forensic details. Conflicts involve catching criminals, internal corruption, or moral dilemmas. Readers want: clever detective work, criminals getting caught, justice served, plot twists about who's guilty. Protagonist should be smart but flawed. High stakes: lives on the line, ticking clocks, personal investment in cases.

Historical.focus: Period setting shapes characters' choices and conflicts. Research the era: clothing, speech patterns, social rules, technology level, major events. Conflicts arise from rigid social hierarchies, limited opportunities (especially for women), political intrigue, war. Readers want: immersion in another time, romance constrained by propriety, characters defying their era's limits, historical events as backdrop. Balance authenticity with modern pacing—don't let period details slow the story. Include: balls, duels, arranged marriages, class tension.

Adventure.focus: Constant movement and discovery. Characters travel to exotic or dangerous locations (jungles, mountains, oceans, ruins). Plot revolves around: treasure hunts, escape from danger, exploration, rescue missions. Action scenes are frequent—chases, fights, natural disasters, traps. Include: maps, artifacts, rival treasure hunters, indigenous guides, dangerous wildlife. Readers want: non-stop excitement, narrow escapes, discovering lost civilizations, overcoming environmental challenges. Pace is rapid—new location every few chapters.

Revenge.focus: Payback is the core motivation. Protagonist was wronged (betrayed, humiliated, robbed, falsely accused) and now seeks justice/vengeance. Structure around targets: take down enemies one by one, from weakest to strongest. Each victory should be satisfying and public—humiliation, exposure, or downfall. Include: secret plans, gathering allies, turning enemy's weapons against them, revealing protagonist's hidden power/identity at perfect moments. Readers want: face-slapping, villains begging for mercy, poetic justice, protagonist's triumph. Emotion: cold satisfaction or hot anger.

Paranormal.focus: Supernatural beings and powers coexist with modern world. Include: vampires, werewolves, witches, ghosts, fae, demons. Establish hierarchy and rules (e.g., vampire weaknesses, pack dynamics, magic costs). Often includes romance between human and supernatural, or between different species. Conflicts involve: hiding from humans, supernatural politics, ancient prophecies, forbidden love. Readers want: discovering hidden supernatural world, protagonist gaining powers, dangerous attraction, battles between supernatural factions. Balance mystery with action.

System.focus: Game-like progression with visible stats, levels, and rewards. Include: status windows, skill trees, experience points, quests, item shops, leveling up. Protagonist starts weak but gains power through completing tasks. Show progression clearly: Level 1 → Level 50, F-rank → S-rank. Each level-up or skill acquisition is a payoff moment. Include: dungeon raids, boss battles, rare loot, hidden quests, ranking competitions. Readers want: frequent upgrades, protagonist becoming overpowered, strategic stat allocation, satisfying number growth. Make system rules clear early.

Reborn.focus: Second chance to fix past mistakes using future knowledge. Protagonist dies/fails in original timeline, returns to earlier point (childhood, young adult, key decision). They remember everything. Core appeal: watching protagonist avoid tragedies, invest early (Bitcoin, stocks), cultivate relationships they neglected, take revenge on those who betrayed them, save loved ones who died. Include: 'I won't make the same mistake' moments, shocking others with future knowledge, butterfly effects, satisfaction of getting it right this time. Balance: not too easy (new challenges arise) but definitely better than first time.

LGBTQ+.focus: Queer relationships and identity at the center. Treat characters as fully realized people whose queerness is important but not their only trait. Include: coming out journeys (if relevant), found family, navigating homophobia/transphobia (if part of story), queer joy and community, diverse queer representation (not just white gay men). Romance should have same emotional beats as any other romance—tension, conflict, resolution. Readers want: authentic representation, happy endings (or bittersweet but hopeful), seeing themselves reflected, avoiding stereotypes. Don't make it trauma-porn; include lightness and love.

Fanfiction.focus: Playing in established universe with existing characters or settings. Respect canon but feel free to diverge (AU, what-if scenarios, fix-it fics). Readers already know these characters—dig deeper into their psychology, explore relationships not developed in original, give them different challenges. Include: canon callbacks, inside jokes, favorite character dynamics, shipping. Common types: canon divergence (X didn't happen), AU (same characters, different world), missing scenes, post-canon continuation. Readers want: more of what they love, closure original didn't provide, characters together (or apart) in ways canon didn't deliver. Balance: familiar enough to recognize, fresh enough to surprise.
